goalsCoverage.gap: The Command Architecture concern defines a strong skeleton (thin RunE -> runX, shared flag registrars, Args validators, one output seam). But three concerns each independently redesign the flag surface and disagree: Global UX makes --quiet/-v/--color/--non-interactive persistent and takes -v; Verbose Logging refuses -v and makes --verbose shorthand-less; Command Architecture keeps --json local. There is no single reconciled flag table, so 'consistent' is asserted by each concern against a different baseline. Until the flag ownership is collapsed into ONE table, consistency is not actually guaranteed.

Covered by Global UX (resolveUX, one-way non-interactive latch, NO_COLOR-supreme) and IO/UX Core (colorprofile.NoTTY at write boundary). The two packages overlap heavily (both define cli/internal/ui, both define New/Config/IsTerminal) and must be merged into one package, but the capability is fully designed.

goalsCoverage.goal: 3. Default status display on long-running commands
goalsCoverage.gap: Progress concern's lifecycle.Reporter widening + Reporter.Run + symmetric Done lines covers this cleanly, with Phase 0 (charm-free) shippable independently.
huh/v2 spinner with verified API lineage, TTY/NO_COLOR/json gating, teardown-on-cancel. Honest indeterminate-spinner-only choice (no fake percentage bars) is correct.

Two concerns specify incompatible -v ergonomics. Global UX: -v is a CountP that ADDITIVELY raises the resolved --log-level (so -vvv steps error<warn<info<debug). Verbose Logging: --verbose is a count with NO shorthand that floors to debug on >=1 (not additive, no -vvv stepping from a higher base). They disagree on (a) whether -v exists at all, (b) additive-step vs binary-floor semantics, (c) the -vvv UX the goal explicitly requests. The goal's literal '-vvv style control' is only delivered by Global UX, but Global UX's -v claim is factually broken (collides with --version). Verbose Logging delivers a safe but goal-incomplete --verbose. Neither, as written, ships the requested -vvv without breaking --version.

goalsCoverage.goal: 6. Non-copyable output to stderr; only script-useful to stdout
goalsCoverage.gap: IO/UX Core and Command Architecture both enumerate the stdout->stderr moves with named test-line migrations, which is good. But (a) the keystone Global UX concern explicitly does NOT own the routing moves and its connect behavior-matrix row mislabels connect as byte-transparent, while connect actually writes banners+KEY=URL interleaved to stdout (verified printConnectStatus -> commandContext.out); (b) IO/UX Core and JSON-Output directly contradict on list's 'No CardanoNetworks found.' line (stderr vs stdout, verified list_test.go:134); (c) the actual routing work is deferred across concerns with no single owner reconciling the contradictions.

goalsCoverage.goal: 7. JSON output where it makes sense
goalsCoverage.gap: Two mutually exclusive flag designs: Global UX + Command Architecture keep --json LOCAL bound to viper key output-json (with YACD_JSON deprecation fallback); JSON-Output concern DROPS --json entirely and ships a single global --output/-o enum bound to YACD_OUTPUT, arguing --json cannot be made env-inert. These cannot both ship. They also disagree on coverage (JSON-Output adds up/down/install/devnet-status shapes; the others only retire the footgun). The honest-reject-unsupported-json behavior also differs (PreRunE reject helper vs not). No reconciliation.

Command Architecture concern is the right spine (runX extraction, cached runtimeConfig, CI guards, no leaf PersistentPreRunE). But cleanliness is undermined by un-deduplicated overlap: two separate cli/internal/ui package designs (UX-flag renderer vs IO core) with conflicting type names (ui.Config vs ui.IO/ui.Policy, New signatures), and four concerns each adding fields to commandContext/RuntimeConfig with overlapping-but-not-identical field sets (ux *ui.UI vs ui *ui.Printer vs uiPolicy ui.Policy; Quiet/Color/Interactive/Verbosity defined in 3 places). Without a merge pass this produces an inconsistent architecture, the opposite of goal 8.

boundaryRisks: FLAG OWNERSHIP IS UNRESOLVED ACROSS CONCERNS (the dominant risk). Global UX registers -v/--verbose as CountP and claims 'no -v collision exists today (verified)' -- this is factually FALSE. Verified empirically with cobra v1.10.2: with Version set, cobra auto-binds -v to --version, so `yacd -v` prints version and exits 0 today (matches root.go:104 Version + root_test.go:28). Global UX's migration (root.go CountP('verbose','v',...)) would silently break the --version shorthand contract. Verbose Logging correctly refuses -v. As written the combined design contains a self-contradiction that violates CLI boundary A (--version predictable, stdout, exit 0).

TWO INCOMPATIBLE JSON FLAG DESIGNS. Global UX/Command Architecture keep --json local bound to output-json (YACD_OUTPUT_JSON) with a YACD_JSON deprecation fallback; JSON-Output drops --json entirely for --output/-o (YACD_OUTPUT). Shipping both produces either two competing flags or a contradiction on the stable JSON-toggle surface. CLI boundary A (machine output stable) and repo invariant (existing --json byte shapes) survive under EITHER, but not under BOTH simultaneously.

TWO OVERLAPPING cli/internal/ui PACKAGE DESIGNS. Global UX defines ui.Config + ui.UI (renderer via colorprofile.Writer); IO/UX Core defines ui.IO + ui.Config (different shape) + ui.New(cfg,in,out,errw); Progress defines ui.Policy + ui.New(stderr,...). Three different New() signatures and three different config types for the SAME package. Without a single owning design this will not compile as a union and breaks repo invariant D's 'charm confined to one place' cleanliness intent (it confines charm but to an internally-contradictory package).

CONNECT STDOUT POLLUTION UNDER-OWNED. Verified printConnectStatus writes 'Forwarding...', the KEY=URL pairs, and 'Wrote... Ctrl-C' ALL to commandContext.out (stdout) via one infoWriter. The keystone Global UX behavior matrix labels connect as byte-transparent (wrong). IO/UX Core and Command Architecture both correctly split (KEY=URL stays stdout, banners to stderr) but disagree in emphasis and neither is the keystone. Risk: the keystone ships first with a wrong connect contract baked into its matrix.

WALLET --ogmios-url/--kupo-url ENV COLLISION is real (verified chainOverridesFromViper reads v.GetString('ogmios-url') -> YACD_OGMIOS_URL under AutomaticEnv) and is ONLY caught by the Command Architecture concern. The other four concerns (including the keystone whose entire job is the YACD_* collision audit) miss it. A `yacd wallet topup` run inside `yacd run` silently inherits the injected YACD_OGMIOS_URL as its --ogmios-url default. If Command Architecture is sequenced last/optional, this host-contract collision (repo invariant D) ships unfixed.

PER-COMMAND timeout/wait ENV BLEED (verified: up/down/install/devnet all read commandContext.viper.GetDuration('timeout'); BindPFlags binds into shared viper so YACD_TIMEOUT/YACD_WAIT apply cross-command) is also ONLY caught by Command Architecture. Same sequencing risk as the wallet collision.

--quiet SEMANTICS DIVERGE. Global UX: --quiet gates UI.Info only, does NOT touch slog level. Verbose Logging: --quiet RAISES the logger threshold to warn. These are opposite decisions on whether -q affects the diagnostic stream. Both claim to be the single resolved Quiet. CLI boundary (meaningful, non-contradictory behavior) needs one answer.

phasingNotes: "The five concerns cannot ship as written because three of them independently redesign the flag/config/ui surface with contradictory specs. Recommended reconciliation before any PR: (1) MERGE the flag+config+ui-construction work into ONE foundation phase that produces a single flag table, a single cli/internal/ui package (one Config, one New, one Reporter), and a single merged commandContext/RuntimeConfig field set. Within it, decide -v (recommend: reassign --version shorthand to none with an explicit test, take -v for verbose with ADDITIVE -vvv stepping, since goal 5 demands -vvv and the additive model is the only one that delivers it), decide --json-vs--output (recommend --output/-o enum per JSON-Output's verified YACD_JSON-inertness argument, which also satisfies goal 7's extensibility, and retire --json with a one-release alias), and decide --quiet's logger effect (recommend Global UX's 'gates UI.Info only, slog untouched' to keep the diagnostic stream single-writer). This foundation phase MUST land the go-list-deps ./cmd import guard (net-new, no guard exists today, verified) and the YACD_* collision fixes (wallet --ogmios-url/--kupo-url and per-command timeout/wait read via cmd.Flags(), both verified-real and currently caught by only one concern). (2) Phase 0 of Progress (charm-free Reporter widening + Run + runInstall signature -> lifecycle.Reporter) can land FIRST and independently, byte-neutral, before the foundation; it is the only genuinely independent early phase. (3) After the foundation: routing phase (single owner, reconciled stdout->stderr table including the connect split and a SINGLE decision on the list empty-state line) with all moved assertions named by file:line; then JSON-shape-addition phase (up/down/install/devnet-status), then charm-styling + spinner + huh-confirm phases. (4) Verbose Logging's slog-only path is a fine INTERIM for the foundation phase (no charm needed for level control), with the charm/log/v2 swap deferred to the styling phase -- but IO/UX Core's immediate log/v2 adoption must yield to that deferral so the import guard and 'first charm PR' story stay coherent. Net: ~6 sequenced phases, each green, but ONLY after a mandatory reconciliation pass collapses the duplicated flag/ui/config designs. As five parallel independently-authored concerns they are NOT directly shippable -- they overlap and contradict on the exact surfaces (flags, ui package, commandContext) that must be singular."
